User: In recent years, retro-style games have seen a significant revival. These games, characterized by pixelated visuals and straightforward mechanics, transport us back to the 1980s and 1990s, an era defined by iconic titles like Pac-Man and Super Mario Bros. Back then, gaming prioritized fundamental mechanics and player engagement over intricate graphics and complex storylines.

Today, as the gaming industry leans heavily toward advanced graphics, virtual reality, and intricate narratives, retro games offer a refreshing simplicity. They appeal not just to older generations, who grew up with these games, but also to newer players seeking gameplay that is both accessible and engaging.

Unity 2D, a widely used game development engine, provides the perfect platform to recreate the magic of these classics while taking advantage of contemporary technology. My project taps into this growing interest by exploring how Unity 2D can be used to design a retro-style game that captures the charm of classic gaming while integrating modern advancements.


A lot of current research on game development is focused on advanced technologies—like realistic 3D graphics, lifelike animations, and AI-driven gameplay. However, research specifically examining retro game design and how modern tools can recreate that charm is relatively limited.

This gap highlights the need to explore how tools like Unity 2D can adapt modern efficiencies, such as streamlined development processes, while staying true to the simplicity and playability of retro games. Projects inspired by titles such as The Sims and other role-playing games provide a starting point for understanding how to blend nostalgia with modern design capabilities effectively.

Despite the rising popularity of retro games, there’s limited guidance on how modern tools can faithfully recreate their simplicity while leveraging contemporary features. Current tools like Unity 2D offer incredible versatility but require thoughtful adaptation to deliver the feel of retro gameplay.

This is where my project, titled My Life, comes in. The game is set in a pixelated 2D world from the 1980s, where players navigate life as their own character. These games, characterized by pixelated visuals and straightforward mechanics, transport us back to the 1980s and 1990s, an era defined by iconic titles like Pac-Man and Super Mario Bros. Back then, gaming prioritized fundamental mechanics and player engagement over intricate graphics and complex storylines.

Today, as the gaming industry leans heavily toward advanced graphics, virtual reality, and intricate narratives, retro games offer a refreshing simplicity. They appeal not just to older generations, who grew up with these games, but also to newer players seeking gameplay that is both accessible and engaging.

Unity 2D, a widely used game development engine, provides the perfect platform to recreate the magic of these classics while taking advantage of contemporary technology. My project taps into this growing interest by exploring how Unity 2D can be used to design a retro-style game that captures the charm of classic gaming while integrating modern advancements.


A lot of current research on game development is focused on advanced technologies—like realistic 3D graphics, lifelike animations, and AI-driven gameplay. However, research specifically examining retro game design and how modern tools can recreate that charm is relatively limited.

This gap highlights the need to explore how tools like Unity 2D can adapt modern efficiencies, such as streamlined development processes, while staying true to the simplicity and playability of retro games. Projects inspired by titles such as The Sims and other role-playing games provide a starting point for understanding how to blend nostalgia with modern design capabilities effectively.

Despite the rising popularity of retro games, there’s limited guidance on how modern tools can faithfully recreate their simplicity while leveraging contemporary features. Current tools like Unity 2D offer incredible versatility but require thoughtful adaptation to deliver the feel of retro gameplay.

This is where my project, titled My Life, comes in. The game is set in a pixelated 2D world from the 1980s, where players navigate life as their own character. The gameplay centers on balancing various aspects of life—work, relationships, and personal growth—while striving to be the best version of themselves.

Inspired by The Sims, My Life aims to recreate a role-playing experience but with simpler mechanics and a nostalgic aesthetic. Key development areas include pixel-based graphics, sprite animations, and basic physics interactions. To stay focused, the project avoids advanced features like AI or multiplayer integration, allowing for a deeper dive into retro-style development challenges and benefits.


The primary objective of My Life is to recreate the spirit of classic retro games using Unity 2D, while also highlighting the efficiency of modern game development tools. The project seeks to bridge the gap between nostalgic gameplay and contemporary design methodologies, providing insights into how retro game design can evolve in today’s landscape.

The target audience includes both seasoned gamers who want to relive the nostalgia of the 1980s and newer players drawn to simple, engaging gameplay. By focusing on the essence of retro gaming—fun, simplicity, and accessibility—My Life aims to deliver an immersive yet straightforward experience.

Ultimately, this project contributes to the field of game development by demonstrating how retro-style games can be reimagined using modern tools, offering game developers and enthusiasts a practical framework for creating similar experiences.


Thank you for your attention. I hope this presentation provided insights into how retro games can merge the nostalgia of the past with the possibilities of the present.
